question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2,000 at 7% per annum rate of interest for the period from 5 February 2023 to 19 April 2023.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total days from 5 Feb to 19 Apr = 23 (Feb) + 31 (Mar) + 19 (Apr) = 73 days.

Time (T) in years = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years.

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

SI = (2000 × 7 × 1/5) ÷ 100 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
 
 5 Feb 2023
 P = ₹2000
 19 Apr 2023
 SI = ₹28
 

 Time = 73 Days (1/5 Year)
 Rate = 7% p.a.

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 7% per annum

Time Period = 5 February 2023 to 19 April 2023

**Time Calculation:**

⇒ Year 2023 is a non-leap year, so February has 28 days.

⇒ Days in February (28 − 5) = 23 days

⇒ Days in March = 31 days

⇒ Days in April = 19 days

⇒ Total Time in days = 23 + 31 + 19 = 73 days

⇒ Time (T) in years = 73 ÷ 365 = 1/5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = [2000 × 7 × (1/5)] ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2000 × 7) ÷ 500

⇒ SI = 14000 ÷ 500

⇒ SI = 28

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Number of Days Calculation Trick

In standard exam interest calculations, either the deposit day or the withdrawal day is counted, but not both. Total days generally sum up to a multiple of 73 (as 365 ÷ 73 = 5). Thus, keep in mind: 73 days = 1/5 year, 146 days = 2/5 year, and 219 days = 3/5 year.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated consistently only on the principal amount over the given duration. Conversely, Compound Interest recalculates interest on both the principal and the previously accumulated interest.

Leap Year Identification

Always verify the year. A year completely divisible by 4 is a leap year (having 29 days in February). For century years (like 1900, 2000), they must be divisible by 400 to be classified as leap years.
